blocks.text: With Yin Fang, Wang Yitong, Li Xueqin
Languages Mandarin Chinese, Japanese With English subtitles

Opening with the unfortunate fate of a shark, which haunts the main character in unique ways, oceans – both physically and metaphorically – play an outsized role in this absurdist father-son drama. Zhong Kaifeng’s ambitious, award-winning film sees its complex sound design play a heightened role, as time and space collapse and blur.
Contains scenes of animal slaughter and graphic violence or injury.
Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

blocks.text: Known for his precise and enigmatic filmmaking, here Lê Bảo crafts a meditative anti-love story revealing fragile connections between humans, sounds and unseen worlds.
The queen of sensual cinema returns with a 1970s Manila-set neo-noir about a police officer-turned-criminal under investigation by her former lover.
Effortlessly moving from one moment to the next, Hyun Lee’s fashionably hip and charming micro-budget debut heralds an exciting directorial talent.
